title: Flag day: port pgpkeys.git into the registry, everyone re-signs
description: Mark 2026-10-22: git-vouch fully replaces gpg and the GPG keyring. One flag day; pgpkeys.git (frozen at a signed commit C) is ported into registry format and everyone re-signs with SSH keys; no dual GPG/SSH period. Research (workflow wf_f4f47132-bc6, 2026-10-22): 645 live keys, ~606 people; 93 can reuse a GPG auth subkey as an accepted SSH key; 1784 verified certifier->key pairs become endorsement drafts; ~80% of maintainers have no GPG key; Linus certifies 2 keys so tiers are not derivable from GPG. Prototype migrate.py + run.sh in the session scratchpad (must be rebuilt as a thin layer that imports git-vouch, not reimplementing verify_person).
design:
DECISIONS (Mark, 2026-10-22):
METARULE 1: don't replace anything git already does; the registry lives in git; read git history instead of inventing records.
METARULE 2: unix tools - add small single-purpose tools rather than growing git-vouch. The migration is its own tool (git-vouch-migrate), the only one that runs gpg.
D3 Duplicate continuity claims: when two person files claim the same pgpkeys fingerprint, check flags both and neither receives GPG-ported endorsement drafts until an anchor resolves it; merge order does not matter.
D4 Old GPG-signed tags: keep gpg for history. pgpkeys.git frozen at C is archived; anyone verifying pre-flag-day tags uses gpg with it. No signed manifest. New work never needs gpg.
D7 Encryption and b4: out of scope. kernel.org keeps a small encryption-only GPG keyring for remail/security lists; b4/patatt later get an openssh keyring exported from the registry; not needed for flag day.
D8 GPG continuity proof (detached GPG signature over the new person file, or reuse of the GPG auth subkey) is required to receive GPG-ported endorsement drafts; grants no tier; registering without it still works (fresh endorsements).
D9 Expired (not revoked) GPG keys are accepted as continuity proof; git-vouch-migrate must handle gpg's EXPKEYSIG status explicitly (untested in research) and test it.
D10 Endorsement drafts are generated locally by each certifier (git-vouch-migrate drafts --as <handle>) from public pgpkeys@C and the registry; never generated centrally or distributed for bulk signing.
Follows from D3 (Claude): person files ported on flag day carry migratedFrom = 'openpgp4fpr:' + 40-hex v4 fingerprint; check validates the format and flags any fingerprint claimed by more than one handle (string comparison, no gpg).
Settled by metarule (Claude, for Mark's review): tier record committed before its person file exists is ignored; retired-key ownership = first commit listing it; revocation by a later-revoked key counts if committed before that key's revocation; all-retired person file is frozen, later changes get the D1 loud warning.
notes:
QUESTION (from vouch-omzm.1 review): git-vouch-migrate port merges keys sharing a UID email when primary names match. A pgpkeys holder can bypass this by copying another holder's name and email onto a newer key, absorbing the victim's draft. Strict alternative: never draft a multi-key group (21 people at af88128 lose a pre-filled draft, drafts 605->~584). Owner's call.
QUESTION (from vouch-omzm.2 review): DESIGN says the auth-subkey proof is 'reuse of that key's authentication subkey as the SSH key'. verify-continuity is stricter: a current, unrevoked listed key equal to the auth subkey must have SIGNED the current people/<h>.json.sig, because the public subkey is public and anyone can list it. Effect: a holder who lists the auth subkey but signs with a backup key, or retires/revokes it later, must use the .asc route instead (pinned by test_auth_subkey_listed_but_not_signing_fails, test_auth_subkey_retired_but_signing_fails, test_auth_subkey_revoked_in_registry_fails). Lenient alternative: listing alone proves it (copy-paste attack). Owner's call; implementation keeps the strict rule until decided.
QUESTION (from vouch-omzm.2 review): DESIGN Flag day step 4 says continuity claims against C are accepted only until the late cutoff, but no tool enforces it. Options: (a) verify-continuity --cutoff DATE rejecting a proof whose person-file version (and .asc) was first committed after DATE, from registry git history (METARULE 1); (b) enforce in drafts --as (omzm.3); (c) policy only: the claim window simply closes because reviewers stop merging .asc files. Also: which date counts (commit vs merge into main). Owner's call; tracked as a bead.
